L34:     cite28†27 L35:     cite29†28 /// Input size at which the round-coefficient routines switch from serial to parallel execution.
L36:     cite30†29 ///
L37:     cite31†30 /// # Why this value
L38:     cite32†31 ///
L39:     cite33†32 /// - Below `2^14` paired elements, the rayon splitting and join overhead outweighs the parallel work.
L40:     cite34†33 /// - Above it, the fold-reduce amortises the splitting cost.
L41:     cite35†34 const PAR_THRESHOLD: usize = 1 << 14;
L42:     cite36†35 L43:     cite37†36 /// Table length from which a threaded suffix binding writes over its own tables.
L44:     cite38†37 ///
L45:     cite39†38 /// # Why this value
L46:     cite40†39 ///
L47:     cite41†40 /// - In place, the blocks of a binding run in levels, one parallel dispatch per level.
L48:     cite42†41 /// - Below `2^23` entries those dispatches cost more than a fresh half-length table.
L49:     cite43†42 /// - Above it, the fresh table's page faults and release dominate instead.
L50:     cite44†43 ///
L51:     cite45†44 /// A table bound in place keeps its buffer, until a round below this length replaces it.
L52:     cite46†45 ///
L53:     cite47†46 /// Without the `parallel` feature there is no dispatch to amortise, so every length
L54:     cite48†47 /// binds in place regardless of this threshold.
L55:     cite49†48 const SUFFIX_IN_PLACE_THRESHOLD: usize = 1 << 23;
L56:     cite50†49 L57:     cite51†50 /// Tile size for the chunked round-coefficient kernel.
L58:     cite52†51 ///
L59:     cite53†52 /// Monty-31 spells out a single-reduction dot product per tile size.
L60:     cite54†53 /// The set of sizes that get one depends on the target:
L61:     cite55†54 ///
L62:     cite56†55 /// ```text
L63:     cite57†56 ///     scalar          every length
L64:     cite58†57 ///     AVX2, AVX-512   2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
L65:     cite59†58 ///     NEON            2, 3, 4, 5, 8
L66:     cite60†59 /// ```
L67:     cite61†60 ///
L68:     cite62†61 /// So `8` is a single-reduction tile on every target.
L69:     cite63†62 /// Binary fields fold the modulus once at any tile size, so the choice is free there.
L70:     cite64†63 ///
L71:     cite65†64 /// - Larger overruns the integer-multiply pipeline depth;
L72:     cite66†65 /// - Smaller dilutes the delayed-reduction win.
L73:     cite67†66 const K: usize = 8;
L74:     cite68†67 L75:     cite69†68 /// Per-tile MAC: extends a `(constant, leading)` accumulator pair.
L76:     cite70†69 ///
L77:     cite71†70 /// # Algorithm
L78:     cite72†71 ///
L79:     cite73†72 /// Folding the active variable in `h(X) = sum_b f(X, b) * w(X, b)` gives:
L80:     cite74†73 ///
L81:     cite75†74 /// ```text
L82:     cite76†75 ///     constant += sum_i  w_lo[i] * e_lo[i]
L83:     cite77†76 ///     leading  += sum_i  (w_hi[i] - w_lo[i]) * (e_hi[i] - e_lo[i])
L84:     cite78†77 /// ```
L85:     cite79†78 ///
L86:     cite80†79 /// where `lo`, `hi` are the two faces of the active variable.
L87:     cite81†80 ///
L88:     cite82†81 /// Each sum is one dot product over `K` pairs, reduced as late as the target permits.
L89:     cite83†82 /// A binary field folds the modulus once for the whole sum.
L90:     cite84†83 /// A Monty-31 packing pays one Montgomery reduction at this tile size on every target.
L91:     cite85†84 #[inline(always)]
L92:     cite86†85 fn chunk_round_step<B, A>(e_lo: &[B; K], e_hi: &[B; K], w_lo: &[A; K], w_hi: &[A; K]) -> (A, A)
L93:     cite87†86 where
L94:     cite88†87 B: PrimeCharacteristicRing + Copy,
L95:     cite89†88 A: Algebra<B> + Copy,
L96:     cite90†89 {
L97:     cite91†90 // Constant term: one delayed-reduction dot product over the b_0 = 0 face.
L98:     cite92†91 let acc0 = A::mixed_dot_product::<K>(w_lo, e_lo);
L99:     cite93†92 L100:     cite94†93 // Materialise the differences (b_0 = 1 minus b_0 = 0) tile-locally so
L101:     cite95†94 // they can feed the same primitive. `K` base subs, no reductions.
L102:     cite96†95 let diffs_e: [B; K] = core::array::from_fn(|i| e_hi[i] - e_lo[i]);
L103:     cite97†96 let diffs_w: [A; K] = core::array::from_fn(|i| w_hi[i] - w_lo[i]);
L104:     cite98†97 L105:     cite99†98 // Leading coefficient: dot product of the differences.
L106:     cite100†99 let acc_inf = A::mixed_dot_product::<K>(&diffs_w, &diffs_e);
L107:     cite101†100 L108:     cite102†101 (acc0, acc_inf)
L109:     cite103†102 }
L110:     cite104†103 L111:     cite105†104 /// Per-pair MAC for the streaming tail (at most `K - 1` leftover pairs).
L112:     cite106†105 #[inline(always)]
L113:     cite107†106 fn round_step<B, A>((acc0, acc_inf): (A, A), e0: B, e1: B, w0: A, w1: A) -> (A, A)
L114:     cite108†107 where
L115:     cite109†108 B: PrimeCharacteristicRing + Copy,
L116:     cite110†109 A: Algebra<B> + Copy,
L117:     cite111†110 {
L118:     cite112†111 (acc0 + w0 * e0, acc_inf + (w1 - w0) * (e1 - e0))
L119:     cite113†112 }
L120:     cite114†113 L121:     cite115†114 /// Splits a `2K`-wide chunk into the two faces of the suffix round variable.
L122:     cite116†115 ///
L123:     cite117†116 /// The suffix variable is the low index bit.
L124:     cite118†117 ///
L125:     cite119†118 /// So the two faces of a point are adjacent entries:
L126:     cite120†119 ///
L127:     cite121†120 /// ```text
L128:     cite122†121 ///     chunk : [ t0, t1, t2, t3, ... ]
L129:     cite123†122 ///     lo    : [ t0, t2, ... ]           the variable at 0
L130:     cite124†123 ///     hi    : [ t1, t3, ... ]           the variable at 1
L131:     cite125†124 /// ```
L132:     cite126†125 #[inline(always)]
L133:     cite127†126 fn gather_pairs<T: Copy>(chunk: &[T]) -> ([T; K], [T; K]) {
L134:     cite128†127 let lo: [T; K] = core::array::from_fn(|i| chunk[2 * i]);
L135:     cite129†128 let hi: [T; K] = core::array::from_fn(|i| chunk[2 * i + 1]);
L136:     cite130†129 (lo, hi)
L137:     cite131†130 }
L138:     cite132†131 L139:     cite133†132 /// Component-wise sum of two `(constant, leading)` accumulator pairs.
L140:     cite134†133 #[inline(always)]
L141:     cite135†134 fn round_reduce<A: Copy + PrimeCharacteristicRing>(a: (A, A), b: (A, A)) -> (A, A) {
L142:     cite136†135 (a.0 + b.0, a.1 + b.1)
L143:     cite137†136 }
L144:     cite138†137 L145:     cite139†138 /// Projective per-tile MAC (eprint 2026/762, Fig. 3).
L146:     cite140†139 ///
L147:     cite141†140 /// Like [`chunk_round_step`], but the tables are interpreted as monomial
L148:     cite142†141 /// coefficients, so the round message is `[s(1), s(inf)]` and the verifier
L149:     cite143†142 /// derives `s(0) := C - s(inf)` from the projective round identity. The
L150:     cite144†143 /// `X = 1` evaluation of a coefficient pair is `lo + hi`, so the differences
L151:     cite145†144 /// of the evaluation basis become sums:
L152:     cite146†145 ///
L153:     cite147†146 /// ```text
L154:     cite148†147 ///     at_one  += sum_i  (w_lo[i] + w_hi[i]) * (e_lo[i] + e_hi[i])
L155:     cite149†148 ///     leading += sum_i  w_hi[i] * e_hi[i]
L156:     cite150†149 /// ```
L157:     cite151†150 #[inline(always)]
L158:     cite152†151 fn chunk_round_step_projective<B, A>(
L159:     cite153†152 e_lo: &[B; K],
L160:     cite154†153 e_hi: &[B; K],
L161:     cite155†154 w_lo: &[A; K],
L162:     cite156†155 w_hi: &[A; K],
L163:     cite157†156 ) -> (A, A)
L164:     cite158†157 where
L165:     cite159†158 B: PrimeCharacteristicRing + Copy,
L166:     cite160†159 A: Algebra<B> + Copy,
L167:     cite161†160 {
L168:     cite162†161 // Materialise the X = 1 evaluations (lo + hi) tile-locally so they can
L169:     cite163†162 // feed the same delayed-reduction primitive. `K` base adds, no reductions.
L170:     cite164†163 let ones_e: [B; K] = core::array::from_fn(|i| e_lo[i] + e_hi[i]);
L171:     cite165†164 let ones_w: [A; K] = core::array::from_fn(|i| w_lo[i] + w_hi[i]);
L172:     cite166†165 L173:     cite167†166 let acc1 = A::mixed_dot_product::<K>(&ones_w, &ones_e);
L174:     cite168†167 L175:     cite169†168 // Leading coefficient: dot product of the high (coefficient) faces.
L176:     cite170†169 let acc_inf = A::mixed_dot_product::<K>(w_hi, e_hi);
L177:     cite171†170 L178:     cite172†171 (acc1, acc_inf)
L179:     cite173†172 }
L180:     cite174†173 L181:     cite175†174 /// Projective per-pair MAC for the streaming tail (no subtraction).
L182:     cite176†175 #[inline(always)]
L183:     cite177†176 fn round_step_projective<B, A>((acc1, acc_inf): (A, A), e0: B, e1: B, w0: A, w1: A) -> (A, A)
L184:     cite178†177 where
L185:     cite179†178 B: PrimeCharacteristicRing + Copy,
L186:     cite180†179 A: Algebra<B> + Copy,
L187:     cite181†180 {
L188:     cite182†181 (acc1 + (w0 + w1) * (e0 + e1), acc_inf + w1 * e1)
L189:     cite183†182 }
L190:     cite184†183 L191:     cite185†184 /// The two prover-sent values of a quadratic sumcheck round.
L192:     cite186†185 ///
L193:     cite187†186 /// The round polynomial has three unknowns; the verifier recovers the third
L194:     cite188†187 /// from the running claim `C`, so only two values cross the transcript. Which
L195:     cite189†188 /// finite point is sent differs by basis:
L196:     cite190†189 ///
L197:     cite191†190 /// | basis      | `c_a`  | `c_inf`  | derived             |
L198:     cite192†191 /// |------------|--------|----------|---------------------|
L199:     cite193†192 /// | evaluation | `h(0)` | `h(inf)` | `h(1) = C - h(0)`   |
L200:     cite194†193 /// | projective | `s(1)` | `s(inf)` | `s(0) = C - s(inf)` |
L201:     cite195†194 ///
L202:     cite196†195 /// The struct itself is basis-agnostic: `c_a` has the same name and type in
L203:     cite197†196 /// both rows, so it carries no evidence of which kernel produced it. What
L204:     cite198†197 /// keeps the rows from being crossed is that a message is only ever produced
L205:     cite199†198 /// by [`Basis::sumcheck_coefficients`] and only ever consumed by
L206:     cite200†199 /// [`Basis::reduce_claim`], each under the same tag.
L207:     cite201†200 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
L208:     cite202†201 pub struct RoundMessage<A> {
L209:     cite203†202 /// The finite-point value: `h(0)` (evaluation basis) or `s(1)` (projective).
L210:     cite204†203 pub c_a: A,
L211:     cite205†204 /// The leading coefficient of the round polynomial: `h(inf)` / `s(inf)`.
L212:     cite206†205 pub c_inf: A,
L213:     cite207†206 }
L214:     cite208†207 L215:     cite209†208 /// Shared prefix round-coefficient scaffold, parameterised over the basis steps.
L216:     cite210†209 ///
L217:     cite211†210 /// The tiling, `PAR_THRESHOLD` par-vs-serial split, and `K`-tail fold are
L218:     cite212†211 /// identical across bases; only the per-tile and per-pair MAC differ. The
L219:     cite213†212 /// evaluation and projective kernels supply their `chunk_step` / `pair_step`
L220:     cite214†213 /// pair so this delicate delayed-reduction loop exists exactly once.
L221:     cite215†214 #[inline]
L222:     cite216†215 fn sumcheck_coefficients_prefix_with<B, A, Chunk, Pair>(
L223:     cite217†216 evals: &[B],
L224:     cite218†217 weights: &[A],
L225:     cite219†218 chunk_step: Chunk,
L226:     cite220†219 pair_step: Pair,
L227:     cite221†220 ) -> (A, A)
L228:     cite222†221 where
L229:     cite223†222 B: PrimeCharacteristicRing + Copy + Send + Sync,
L230:     cite224†223 A: Algebra<B> + Copy + Send + Sync,
L231:     cite225†224 Chunk: Fn(&[B; K], &[B; K], &[A; K], &[A; K]) -> (A, A) + Sync,
L232:     cite226†225 Pair: Fn((A, A), B, B, A, A) -> (A, A),
L233:     cite227†226 {
L234:     cite228†227 // Precondition: paired slices must be aligned; half-and-half split addresses the prefix bit.
L235:     cite229†228 assert_eq!(evals.len(), weights.len());
L236:     cite230†229 assert!(evals.len().is_multiple_of(2));
L237:     cite231†230 let half = evals.len() / 2;
L238:     cite232†231 let (e_lo, e_hi) = evals.split_at(half);
L239:     cite233†232 let (w_lo, w_hi) = weights.split_at(half);
L240:     cite234†233 L241:     cite235†234 let body = (half / K) * K;
L242:     cite236†235 let (e_lo_main, e_lo_tail) = e_lo.split_at(body);
L243:     cite237†236 let (e_hi_main, e_hi_tail) = e_hi.split_at(body);
L244:     cite238†237 let (w_lo_main, w_lo_tail) = w_lo.split_at(body);
L245:     cite239†238 let (w_hi_main, w_hi_tail) = w_hi.split_at(body);
L246:     cite240†239 L247:     cite241†240 // Main chunked loop: K pairs per iteration via delayed-reduction dot products.
L248:     cite242†241 let main: (A, A) = if half > PAR_THRESHOLD {
L249:     cite243†242 e_lo_main
L250:     cite244†243 .par_chunks_exact(K)
L251:     cite245†244 .zip(e_hi_main.par_chunks_exact(K))
L252:     cite246†245 .zip(
L253:     cite247†246 w_lo_main
L254:     cite248†247 .par_chunks_exact(K)
L255:     cite249†248 .zip(w_hi_main.par_chunks_exact(K)),
L256:     cite250†249 )
L257:     cite251†250 .par_fold_reduce(
L258:     cite252†251 || (A::ZERO, A::ZERO),
L259:     cite253†252 |acc, ((e_lo_c, e_hi_c), (w_lo_c, w_hi_c))| {
L260:     cite254†253 let chunk = chunk_step(
L261:     cite255†254 e_lo_c.try_into().unwrap(),
